  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stimulation Paradigm as the independent factor.",
    "For 'Success', which is binary (0/1), treat it as a continuous variable for ANOVA but note the violation of normality; alternatively, consider a Chi-square test of independence or Logistic Regression as a robust alternative if normality assumptions fail.",
    "For 'AD', verify normality of residuals; if skewed, apply a logit or arcsine transformation before ANOVA.",
    "Check homogeneity of variances (Levene's test) for all five models."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any ANOVA yields a significant F-statistic (p < 0.05), conduct pairwise comparisons between all five stimulation paradigms.",
    "Calculate mean differences and 95% confidence intervals for each pair.",
    "Report adjusted p-values to control family-wise error rate."
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Bonferroni correction",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Since the response variables are continuous (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) but 'Success' is binary, an Ordinary Linear Regression (OLR) is inappropriate for 'Success'. For 'Success', a Logistic Regression (or Multinomial Logistic Regression if treating success as a categorical outcome) is recommended. For the continuous variables, OLR is appropriate if assumptions are met. A unified approach could involve a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with appropriate link functions for each variable, or separate models per variable type.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality of residuals for continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) checked via Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk test.",
    "Homogeneity of variances across the five stimulation paradigms checked via Levene's test.",
    "Independence of observations (verified by dataset structure: 76,655 rows from 8 mice, implying repeated measures; if mice are nested within paradigms, a Mixed Effects Model with 'Mouse' as a random effect is required instead of standard ANOVA).",
    "Linearity and lack of multicollinearity for regression models.",
    "For 'Success', check for binomial distribution fit rather than normality."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Based on summary statistics, 'Sham' is expected to show significantly lower Success rates (mean=0.27) and higher Time-to-Target (mean=4.68) compared to other paradigms.",
    "Visual paradigms (Bright Visual Only, Dim Visual Only) and Combined are expected to outperform ICMS Only and Sham in Success and Path Efficiency.",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) is expected to be lowest in Sham (0.236) and highest in Combined (0.399), suggesting different navigation strategies or stability.",
    "Average Speed is expected to be lowest in Sham (10.74) and highest in Combined (12.83).",
    "Time-to-Target is expected to be longest in Sham (4.68) and shortest in Combined (2.56)."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset includes repeated measures (multiple trials per mouse); standard ANOVA assumes independence, potentially inflating Type I error unless a Mixed Effects Model is used.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary, violating the normality assumption of standard ANOVA.",
    "Potential outliers in 'Time-to-Target' (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81) and 'Path Efficiency' (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) may skew results.",
    "Unequal sample sizes across paradigms (Sham n=3505 vs Combined n=48846) may affect power and balance.",
    "No information on mouse-level random effects is provided in the summary, making it difficult to fully account for inter-mouse variability without raw data access."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a Linear Mixed Effects Model (LMM) for continuous variables and a Generalized Linear Mixed Effects Model (GLMM) with a binomial link for 'Success', including 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for repeated measures, followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons with Bonferroni correction."
}
